doc.title: Harry Allen interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 13, 1997

title: Burrillville High School and Major Holley, Oliver Jackson
summary: Small high school jazz band, All Star RI band at Newport; Major Holley had him sit in at sixteen and introduced Oliver Jackson, source of European tours.

bands.name: All Star Rhode Island High School Jazz Band

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. The high school I went to was a small high school called Burrillville High School in Burrillville, Rhode Island. It was a very small town and a very small high school, but we had a fairly decent music department and we had a jazz band. And there was also, in addition to the All State music circuit they had, there was a band called the All Star Rhode Island High School Jazz Band and I played in that and we got to play at the Newport Jazz Festival and a couple of other places, so that was a lot of fun.
Did you get to rub elbows with any well known arranger/conductors at that time?

Not really at that point. I had met Scott Hamilton and Warren Vache and Major Holly and some people like that. Major Holly was very, very supportive and had me come down and sit in with him in New York when I was sixteen. And he later on introduced me to Oliver Jackson, who was the first guy to take me on tour — he took me on a bunch of tours around Europe which ended up accounting for probably about half of the work I © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-
do now, from tours that can be traced directly back to the contacts I made through Oliver Jackson.
